llm.summary: The package is a coherent Polymarket trading client, but the marketplace metadata omits the sensitive environment and file access the code actually needs and performs (private keys, .env loading, on-disk API-cred caching), which is a meaningful mismatch users should be aware of.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md consistently implement a Polymarket trading skill (placing market/limit orders, querying balances, multi-account support). However the registry metadata claims no required environment variables or primary credential while the code expects account private keys and funder addresses in pmbuysell/.env (PM_ACCOUNT_IDS, ACCx_PRIVATE_KEY, ACCx_FUNDER or PM_ACCOUNTS_JSON). It also expects optional builder/relayer creds for redeem. The missing metadata declaration of sensitive env vars is an incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs agents to create/edit pmbuysell/.env containing private keys and to run pip install -r pmbuysell/requirements.txt. The runtime code reads those env vars and will load a project-level .env fallback. The skill only contacts expected endpoints (Polymarket gamma-api and the CLOB host) and does not contain obvious network exfil endpoints, but it does cache derived API credentials to disk under pmbuysell/data. The instructions give the agent permission to create/modify .env and run CLIs that will read/write these sensitive items.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in the registry, but SKILL.md tells operators to pip install the package's requirements (pmbuysell/requirements.txt). The code imports third-party libraries (py_clob_client, requests, python-dotenv). Installing pip deps is normal but carries moderate risk — you should inspect requirements.txt and the provenance of those packages before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires storing and reading high-value secrets (private keys, funder addresses, and optional builder API credentials) in pmbuysell/.env or PM_ACCOUNTS_JSON, yet the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. The code also uses load_dotenv(override=True) and will load both pmbuysell/.env and a fallback project-level .env, which can expose unrelated environment variables. The skill derives and caches ApiCreds (api_key, api_secret, api_passphrase) to files under pmbuysell/data, persisting sensitive credentials to disk.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good) but the skill persists sensitive data locally: it writes a .env template, may read/override project-level .env, and caches derived API credentials to files under pmbuysell/data (filename polymarket_api_creds_*.json). Autonomous invocation combined with access to wallet private keys and persisted API creds increases blast radius if the skill or environment is later compromised.

llm.guidance:
This package implements a Polymarket trading client and requires private keys and funder addresses in pmbuysell/.env (or PM_ACCOUNTS_JSON), but the registry metadata does not declare those requirements — that's the main mismatch. Before installing or using this skill: 

- Do not put high-value wallet private keys in a shared or long-lived machine environment; use a dedicated/deposit-only wallet with minimal funds for automated agents. 
- Inspect pmbuysell/requirements.txt and verify the provenance of third-party packages (especially py_clob_client). 
- Be aware the code will load both pmbuysell/.env and a parent-project .env and uses load_dotenv(override=True) which can override environment variables unexpectedly. 
- The skill caches derived API credentials to files under pmbuysell/data (polymarket_api_creds_*.json). Ensure file permissions are appropriate or avoid persistent storage if you can't protect the host. 
- If you need auditability, review the full source (already included) for any additional network calls, and consider running in an isolated environment (container or ephemeral VM). 

If you trust the author and intend to use the skill, limit the keys you give it and confirm requirements.txt contents; if you don't trust the package or cannot isolate secrets, do not install or run it.
